[[Stadion Balgarska Armia|Bulgarian Army Stadium]] (under construction) | capacity = 43,230 | owntitle = Owner | owner = [[Valter Papazki]] | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Markus Gisdol]] | current = 2026–27 PFC CSKA Sofia season | league = [[First Professional Football League|First League]] | season = [[2025–26 First Professional Football League (Bulgaria)|2025–26]] | position = First League, 4th of 16 | website = {{Official URL}} | pattern_la1 = _cskasofia26-27h | pattern_b1 = _cskasofia26-27h | pattern_ra1 = _cskasofia26-27h | pattern_sh1 = _cskasofia26-27h | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = FFFFFF | body1 = DD0000 | rightarm1 = FFFFFF | shorts1 = DD0000 | socks1 = FF0000 | pattern_la2 = _cskasofia26-27a | pattern_b2 = _cskasofia26-27a | pattern_ra2 = _cskasofia26-27a | pattern_sh2 = _cskasofia26-27a | pattern_so2 = | shorts2 = FFFFFF | socks2 = FFFFFF | pattern_la3 = _macronwyverneco24ba | pattern_b3 = _macronwyverneco24ba | pattern_ra3 = _macronwyverneco24ba | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so3 = | shorts3 = 000000 | socks3 = 000000 }} {{USC CSKA Sofia}} '''PFC CSKA Sofia''' ({{langx|bg|ПФК ЦСКА София}}) ({{audio|Bg-CSKA Sofia.ogg|pronunciation}}) is a Bulgarian professional [[association football]] club based in [[Sofia]] and currently competing in the country's premier football competition, the [[First Professional Football League|First League]]. ''CSKA'' is an abbreviation for ''Central Sports Club of the Army'' ({{langx|bg|Централен Спортен Клуб на Армията}}). Officially established on 5 May 1948, CSKA's roots date back to an [[OSK AS-23|army officers' club]] founded in 1923.{{cite web |url=https://www.dnes.bg/a/9-sport/79567-sadat-prizna-tsska-e-naslednik-na-as-23 |title=Court: CSKA is the official successor to AS-23 | publisher=dnes.bg | date=21 October 2009}} The club has won a record 31 [[Bulgarian A Professional Football Group|Bulgarian titles]] and 22 [[Bulgarian Cup]]s.{{cite web |url=https://www.bta.bg/en/news/sport/1130460-cska-sofia-claim-22nd-bulgarian-cup-title |title=CSKA Sofia Claim 22nd Bulgarian Cup | publisher=BTA|date=21 May 2026}} Internationally, CSKA are the only Bulgarian club to have reached the semi-finals of the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]], which they have done twice,[https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/history/clubs/50076--cska-sofia/ UEFA Champions League – History – CSKA Sofia] ''UEFA.com'' Retrieved 23 May 2026. and they have also reached the semi-final of the [[1988–89 European Cup Winners' Cup|UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]] once. CSKA's home colors are red and white and its home ground is the [[Stadion Balgarska Armia|Bulgarian Army Stadium]]. The club's biggest rivals are [[PFC Levski Sofia|Levski Sofia]] and matches between the two sides are known as [[The Eternal Derby]]."}}
